name: Sherman Brandson
deck: Wherever Dorren Skura went, he was under center: Baltimore, Tampa Bay, New York. He waited out the lean years in Minnesota until the coach came back, threw for more yards and touchdowns than anyone the league has seen, and in Y95 finally handed over the crown.

chapters.headline: Baltimore, Where the Long Ball Became a Habit
body: Sherman Brandson's first rings came in Baltimore, on a Ravens club Dorren Skura had already turned into a machine. Y46 set the tone: 16-0-1 in the regular season and a 32-24 win over the Seahawks in Super Bowl CV. In week 3 of that season he found D. Haley for a 77-yard touchdown against the Browns, still the longest passing play on Skura's record board.

The Ravens went 17-0 in Y48 and beat the Rams 16-9, then 16-1 in Y49 and beat the Eagles 36-28. Y50 was the one that got away: another 17-0 regular season, a 58-yard touchdown run by Denzel Hayes on a Brandson handoff against the Dolphins that is still the longest on the board, and a 36-32 loss to the Saints in Super Bowl CIX. He left Baltimore with 3 rings, and Baltimore has since retired his number.

chapters.headline: Tampa Bay, and a Title Won Against His Old Club
body: When Skura moved to Tampa Bay for Y51, Brandson moved too, and the Buccaneers did not lose a step. They went 16-1 and routed the Jaguars 40-13 in Super Bowl CX. A year later they went 16-1 again and met the Ravens in Super Bowl CXI, Brandson against the club where he had won his first rings. Tampa Bay won 32-25.

Y53 was the cruelest season of his prime. The Buccaneers went 17-0, the only perfect regular season of his three in Tampa Bay, and still went out in the championship round. The Titans won that title instead, 36-31 over the Eagles, and Brandson's run of titles stopped at two in Tampa Bay.

chapters.headline: New York, and the Season Nobody Has Come Close To
body: Skura took the Giants job for Y54 and Brandson was under center again. The Giants went 16-1 and beat the Jets 36-28 in Super Bowl CXIII. Then came Y55, the season that still defines him. He threw 94 touchdown passes, the most in a season on Skura's record board, and nothing in the league's tracked seasons since has come within 22 of it; Bones Crawford's 72 in Y89 is the nearest. Nine of them came in a single game against the Chiefs, the club the Giants beat 68-21 in Super Bowl CXIV.

He played three seasons in New York and is remembered first as a Giant. Y56 made it three titles in three years: a 14-2-1 season and a 38-37 escape against the Bills in Super Bowl CXV. The club has retired his number and keeps him in its Ring of Honor beside Jackson Wardell Kline.

chapters.headline: Minnesota: The Long Wait, Two More Rings, and an Unfinished Chase
body: Brandson spent Y57 through Y60 in Minnesota without a ring while Skura won three straight titles in Miami. Then, for Y61, the coach came to the Vikings, and the old partnership picked up as if it had never stopped. The Vikings went 12-5 and beat the Ravens 40-14 in Super Bowl CXX, another title won against Baltimore. They went 14-3 in Y62 and beat the Jaguars 40-24, 40 points in both Super Bowls.

Y62 was also his last season, and it ended too early. Injury cut it short while he was on pace for the best passing season on Skura's record board, Dennis Baylon's 7,452 yards from Y33, a mark that still stands. The same season his receiver God Johnson, then Mason Earl III, caught for 4,247 yards, still the best receiving season on the board. Y62 is also where the board dates both of Brandson's career marks: 91,463 passing yards and 1,150 touchdown passes. He retired a Viking with 10 rings. Minnesota, New York and Baltimore all retired his number.

chapters.headline: Michael Wilson, the Quarterback Who Inherited Minnesota
body: Michael Wilson, "Air Wilson", never shared a huddle with Brandson. He spent Y60 through Y62 in Baltimore without a ring while Brandson was finishing in Minnesota, then took over the Vikings for Y63, the season after injury ended Brandson's career. The dynasty did not miss a beat: Wilson won 5 rings there in six seasons, throwing to God Johnson, who set the career receiving record on Skura's board in Y67. Side by side, the careers are not close. Wilson completed 72 percent of his passes, Brandson 84.7. Wilson threw for 58,992 yards and 690 touchdowns in 214 games; Brandson for 91,463 and 1,150 in 315. Wilson won 6 MVPs, Brandson 8. Both now hang in Minnesota's Ring of Honor.

chapters.headline: The Most Valuable Card in the League, Until Y95
body: Brandson has not thrown a pass in the market's lifetime, and his card has still climbed. It was valued at 36,912 after Y80 and 40,388 after Y94, rated 99 with an A+ grade the whole way, the most valuable card in the league at every season's end. Each new season rescales Career Legacy, and a frozen line like his only looks better against it. Y95 was the first time another card finished above it: Ryland Maxwell's, at 44,400 to his 40,657.

chapters.headline: The Numbers
body: In 315 games: 91,463 passing yards, 1,150 touchdown passes at 3.65 a game, 84.7 percent of his passes completed and only 50 sacks taken. 10 rings, 8 MVPs and 4 Super Bowl MVPs. No Offensive Player of the Year award ever came, the one gap on a shelf full of MVPs.

chapters.headline: Y95, the Year the Crown Changed Hands
body: For as long as the market has measured it, Brandson held the top Career Legacy in the league. After Y94 he led Ryland Maxwell by 381. Maxwell added 912 in Y95 and finished it at 14,019, 479 ahead of Brandson's 13,540. The passing records are another matter. His 91,463 yards lead Wayne Wilson, "The Mailman", by 1,013, his 1,150 touchdown passes lead by 237, and the Hall of Fame ballot scored his case at 100, a perfect mark only Rondale Ikarras and God Johnson share.
